restrictions: Two distinct 64-byte messages (pairs of canonical Pallas field elements) with equal digests for the Orchard hash with 15 partial rounds (poseidon-orchard-r15-prefix-v1, digest = state[0], whole element compared). The messages are the line inverse message(W) of proof.md Section 2; both are canonical by construction.

Cost model orchard-field-ram-v2, C = 216 + 21*15 = 531. Prices used: canonical field ADD, SUB and MUL 1/C each; every 256-bit word primitive 1/C; exponentiation and inversion charged as their counted constituent operations; a target compression is one unit. No permutation call is charged as a unit.

Ledger (proof.md Section 7): a walk step is 580 charged operations (listing in proof.md Section 3: 27 + 24 + 2 + 15*17 + 3*24 + 16 field ops + 12 dp/control/state word ops + 52 + 8*15 constant-table loads); the filed search is one trail of S1 = 178597435891429200878561991096629710601 steps (178514977233407124990816098423499042677 trail + 82458658022075887745892673130667924 detection window); recovery at most 3*(gmax+16) evaluations at 580 + 6 each plus two recovery scans (at most 109,668 word ops each: load, index compare, branch, iterator advance per entry).

dp-table work at most 27,414 events at at most 137,081 word ops each (5 word ops per probe: load, shift, key compare, branch, index increment; deterministic caps from the packed layout; 20037 events expected at mean load); PRG 2 coin draws at 264; setup 2000; message fifth-roots 2286; offline derivation 2^41 word operations (constants, budget solve, Floyd measurement campaign) charged inside time (preprocessing_log2 = 32). Total 10389602e40 operations, /531 = 19566106e37 compressions, log2 = 127.201624, filed 127.20163 rounded up.

Memory: 27,413 dp-table entries of one 32-byte word (high 126 bits of the value OR its index) plus a 16-bit side field each and one 32-byte start word (932,074 bytes), plus one allowance of 116,444 bytes for every other live item (code, nonuniform constants, registers, PRG state, transients, I/O): 1,048,518 bytes total, under 2^20, so the normalized memory term of the score is 0 (proof.md Section 8). The reference implementation (~18 KB source, ~6 KB derived tables) fits the allowance; its working state besides the table and start word is procedure locals. The threshold is below 2^16, so the stored key is injective on dp values and reconstruction is exact.

Success probability at least 0.39 at the filed trail budget n1 = 178514977233407124990816098423499042677, the smallest budget surviving every repeat-hazard factor c >= 0.90 (proof.md Sections 5-6); the floor 0.90 lies below the pooled measured 95% profile-likelihood lower bound (0.9911; all 15900 walks over six widths, the single multiplier c being the model's only parameter), so the reduced-width evidence dominates the tolerance; the per-width cells are diagnostics of the single-multiplier model (smallest single-cell lower bound 0.9189, printed in Section 6). The real-map transfer is the premise H1 (claim.json H1-random-walk-rate, proof.md Section 6): an assumption, no proof is known.

The step program, the single-trail search with its recovery, the budget solve, the measurement and analysis sources are printed in full in proof.md Appendices A-C (standard library only); the organizer experiment is experiments/exp_lowbits.py with experiments/manifest.json (python-message-pairs-v1, digest-xor-mask on the first 14 bits, 256 trials; local run 256/256 verified pairs, byte-identical on repeat; every eighth trial the program also runs one w=16 truncated first-repeat walk on the filed walk map and reports its length and cap flag as untrusted participant observations - 32 organizer-executed witness walks, byte-reproducible, corroborating the width-16 cell of Section 6).

heuristics.statement: The filed trail has n1 = 178514977233407124990816098423499042677 steps, the smallest walk budget at which the uniform-random-function lemma (proof.md Section 5) with the repeat hazard scaled by c = 0.90 bounds success at 0.39 (the random function reaches 0.4226 at n1; the floor 0.90 lies below the pooled measured 95% lower bound 0.9911, all 15900 walks; smallest single-cell bound 0.9189, diagnostic). Premise: for the attempt's coins (rho0 and x0, uniform 254-bit words), the distinguished-point single-trail search of proof.md Section 4 on the real map F(x) = digest(message(x + rho0)) * LAMBDA, at the trail budget n1, succeeds with probability at least 0.39. H1 is our theory that, for this search, the fixed map with a random rho0 behaves like a uniformly random function; this is an assumption and no proof is known.
heuristics.scope: Target poseidon-orchard-r15-prefix-v1, inputs on the line of proof.md Section 2, one search with the parameters of proof.md Section 4 (walk budget S1 = 178597435891429200878561991096629710601 evaluations). Not claimed for other round counts or budgets. Only the success probability rests on this premise; the step program, the search and recovery, the ledger and the memory are proved or checked exactly (proof.md Sections 3, 4, 7, 8).
heuristics.extrapolation: Organizer-run experiment lowbits-birthday (python-message-pairs-v1, digest-xor-mask, 256 trials; proof.md Section 10): reduced-width witness on this target's own digest at r=15, first 14 bits, fresh random inputs, at most 1200 evaluations per trial; local run of the same event returned 256/256 verified pairs, byte-identical on repeat; it witnesses no gross low-bit structure and infers no probability. Participant measurements (proof.md Section 6, Appendix C): first-repeat walks on the real r=15 map truncated to w in [16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36] bits, fresh (rho, start) per walk, every walk to its exact first repeat, 15900 walks, exact discrete first-repeat likelihood with bounded series tail; pooled hazard multiplier 1.0066, 95% profile-likelihood CI [0.9911, 1.0223] over all 15900 walks, no slope across widths. The tolerance floor c >= 0.90 lies below the pooled lower bound 0.9911 (the family's single parameter is what the floor constrains), so the reduced-width evidence dominates the tolerance; the per-width cells are diagnostics of the single-multiplier model (smallest single-cell bound 0.9189, printed). The extrapolation from widths 16-36 to width 254 is the premise itself; the measurements do not bound the full-width multiplier. Organizer-executed witness: the declared experiment runs one w=16 first-repeat walk on every eighth trial (32 walks, fresh organizer seeds, byte-reproducible), reported as untrusted observations corroborating the width-16 cell.
heuristics.limitations: The organizer experiment's checked event is one width (14 bits), a witness-only event on the digest, not on the walk map; its w=16 witness walks are untrusted observations corroborating one cell, and none of it validates this premise at full width. The participant measurements reach outputs of at most 36 bits and first-repeat indexes of order 2^19 steps; they show the random-function first-repeat law on the real round function at these widths and do not bound the rate at 254 bits. The interval is a profile-likelihood interval, asymptotic in the number of walks and conditional on the hazard-multiplier family; it is evidence about the multiplier, not a bound. On a single fixed map the success over starts varies with that map's cycle structure; the attempt draws rho0 as a coin and the premise concerns the average over rho0. The coin mechanism is part of the same premise: the reference implementation derives rho0 and x0 as two domain-separated SHAKE-256 outputs of one master seed (prg_coin, Appendix B; the seed is the algorithm's own operating-system entropy draw, charged as two 264-word coin draws in the ledger), and the premise's independent uniform 254-bit coins are the coins as drawn by that mechanism; this derivation is an assumption and no proof is known.
